title: Pair-validity machine
statement: There is a deterministic Boolean Turing machine with no work tapes and state set $\mathrm{Option}(\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\})$, initially in the state representing no stored Boolean. From that state, on input $b$ it moves right, emits nothing, and stores $b$. When it has stored $b$ and reads $c$, it moves right: if $b=c$, it emits nothing and returns to the state with no stored Boolean; if $b\ne c$, it emits $\neg b\land c$ and halts. On blank in either kind of state, it emits false and halts without moving.
